results.what: Determination of the logarithmic decrement of a swinging magnet. Logs of successive amplitudes are averaged over blocks of 5 swings, and the difference of block means is divided by the number of intervening swings (17).
results.modern_name: logarithmic decrement of a damped oscillator (block-mean estimate of the slope of log amplitude)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber, magnetic observations 1836–37 (Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins); damping theory developed by Gauss and W. Weber

results.what: Comparison of damping with the circuit open versus closed, isolating the damping due to induced currents (0.00218 vs 0.00761 per swing).
results.modern_name: electromagnetic (eddy/induction) damping of a galvanometer/magnetometer; basis of later absolute resistance measurement
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and W. Weber (1830s); Weber's later damping-based absolute resistance determinations (1850s)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine raw laboratory record of the Gauss–Weber induction and damping experiments, which are well documented. The arithmetic (logarithms, block means, logarithmic decrement) is standard for Gauss's magnetometric practice. Its only interest is as primary data.

checkable.asserts: Logs of the first open-circuit group: 3.10486, 3.10278, 3.10066 (Gauss 3.10067), 3.09845, 3.09628.
Equals 2.890196, confirming that the second entry is 2.89793.
Oscillation period ≈ 42.36–42.37 s, consistent across groups and circuit states.
